narration_use: reference only when drafting; required units must be derivable from the public B2 inputs (table + intent)
file_naming: one G1 per input contract; B1/B3/B4/B5 need separate drafts
intent: To illustrate the projected severe rise in global average temperature by 2100 and warn of the catastrophic consequences of global inaction.

units.meaning: The chart tracks a single metric, 'Change in average global temperature', measured in degrees Celsius, spanning 1883 to 2019.

basis.note: first row establishes series label and unit degC

accepted_routes: single temperature-change series in degrees Celsius
units.visual_evidence_rule: The series name and unit must be visible or clearly labeled.
units.temporal_anchor: opening narration clause introducing the warming data
units.reviewer_question: Must the video display the metric name and unit?

units.meaning: By 2019 the series reaches its highest value in the table, 0.946 °C, just under one degree of warming.

basis.note: final and maximum value in the table

accepted_routes: just under one degree Celsius at the end of the series
units.visual_evidence_rule: The final data point must be visibly marked or labeled with its 2019 value.
units.temporal_anchor: the clause 'just one degree of warming'
units.reviewer_question: Must the final value be shown as the series endpoint?

units.meaning: From 1883 to 2019 the series rises by about 1.10 °C, from -0.156 °C to 0.946 °C.
accepted_routes: from about -0.16 °C in 1883 to about 0.95 °C in 2019
an increase of about 1.10 °C across the series
units.visual_evidence_rule: Both the first and final data points must be visible enough to show the total change.
units.temporal_anchor: the clause 'just one degree of warming' or the opening trend setup
units.reviewer_question: Must the total rise from start to end be conveyed?

units.meaning: The steepest rise occurs in recent decades: from 0.198 °C in 1980 to 0.946 °C in 2019, an increase of about 0.75 °C.
accepted_routes: the last four decades add about 0.75 °C
from about 0.2 °C in 1980 to about 0.95 °C in 2019
units.visual_evidence_rule: The upward slope must visibly steepen after 1980, with the 1980 and 2019 values identifiable.
units.temporal_anchor: the clause about the world being on track to warm further
units.reviewer_question: Must the video emphasize the recent acceleration in warming?

units.meaning: The series first becomes positive in 1941 at 0.052 °C, but remains continuously positive only from 1976 onward, at 0.032 °C in 1976.

basis.note: first positive value in the table
last negative value before sustained positive period

accepted_routes: crosses from negative to positive territory, then stays positive after the mid-1970s
units.visual_evidence_rule: The baseline crossing and later sustained positive region must be visible in the series shape.
units.temporal_anchor: historical context clause before the modern warming trend
units.reviewer_question: Is this baseline-crossing nuance required or optional?

optional_valid: Early period is below baseline with a minimum of -0.432 °C in 1911.
The series is not monotonic; it has temporary reversals and fluctuations around the baseline.
The 2100/3 °C projection from the narration is external context and, if shown, must be clearly separated from the table's historical data.
unsupported_to_avoid: Plotting 3 °C by 2100 as a data value, since the table ends in 2019.
Encoding catastrophic consequences as data values or causal claims.
Using relative_value as a percentage, share, or count.
Extrapolating beyond the table's last year without labeling it as external narration.
Claiming the table shows the 2100 projection directly.
notes: All numeric claims are drawn from the table's value column in degC. The 2100/3 °C projection in the narration is not present in the table and should not be encoded as a data unit.
weight_mode_note: every unit gets 1/n so coverage is a plain share; weight_template is kept for per-type analysis only
